models.title: Pearson chi-square statistic for a contingency table
models.summary: Pearson contingency-table chi-square adds each cell squared observed-minus-expected residual divided by its expected count.

relationship.locator: Section7.4.5, Test statistic and Degrees of freedom
relationship.translation_notes: All observation counts are dimensionless. Prebinding the complete cell contributions permits a sum without unsupported two-index mapping. Degrees of freedom have their own quantity definition; a sample-variance chi-square statistic is a distinct target. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: One nonnegative squared count residual divided by positive expected count for every cell
variables.context: One r by c contingency table, mutually exclusive categories and independently sampled classified observations
Same table and independence-null expected-cell convention

assumptions: Bind every cell exactly once, withE_ij>0 and expected counts based on the independence null; observed counts are nonnegative integers.
Chi-square reference distribution is an asymptotic approximation requiring suitable expected-cell sizes and the proper independent sampling design.
limitations: No Yates continuity correction, structural-zero adjustment, exact test, or Monte Carlo p-value is included.
The finite-family guard cannot verify each bound contribution or the consistency of the original table margins.

models.title: Pearson residual of an observed contingency-table cell
models.summary: A Pearson cell residual preserves the sign of the discrepancy and scales it by the square root of expected count.

relationship.translation_notes: Counts are dimensionless, and the residual is a signed dimensionless diagnostic. Squaring and summing all such residuals recovers the uncorrected Pearson chi-square statistic. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.context: One contingency-table cell and its independence-null expected frequency

variables.definition: Signed observed-minus-expected count scaled by sqrt(expected)

assumptions: Expected frequency must be strictly positive and correspond to this cell and sampling/null model.
Observed frequency is an integer>=0; expected need not be an integer.
limitations: The book calls this standardized; it is the Pearson residual, which differs from the adjusted standardized residual using estimated cell variance.
